what_happened: The the person running Athena closed queued item 7ym7 by hand while drain-43 was already reading it. The drain's reading commit was refused by the gate, because the outcome said 0 invocations but one invocation record existed. The item counted as failed twice and the drain stopped before it ran any job. No work was judged bad.
cause: Athena lets a hand command change a queued item's state while a drain is running, and it does not check whether the drain holds the item. The close command does not look for a running drain or an item being read. The drain does not guard against its item changing under it, and it reports the clash only as a gate refusal. Safe use depends on the the person running Athena remembering to stop the drain first. The same shared-state clash happened before, when a hand command changed the working copy that drain uses.
prevention: The close command (and other hand commands that change a queued item) should check for a running drain and for the item's in-flight state. If a drain holds the item, the command should refuse and say to run drain-stop first or wait. A fallback is for the drain to recognise an item closed under it, drop it as retired and carry on, instead of counting it failed and stopping. The refusal check would have prevented this whole class.
proposed_request: Make the commands that close or change a queued item safe while a drain is running. (1) Before closing an item, `athena close` must check whether a drain is running and whether it has picked or is reading that item. If so, it must refuse with a message naming the drain and saying to run drain-stop first or wait. (2) If an item is found closed while the drain is working on it, the drain must record it as retired, drop it, and carry on to the next item. It must not count it as failed or stop. (3) Add tests for both cases: closing an item a running drain has picked is refused, and an item closed under the drain is retired without stopping it. Acceptance: with a drain reading item X, closing X by hand is refused and the drain continues; the drain's reading commit is never refused because of a hand close.
